raw_response:
I have farmed these 13.1 mu in Quzhou for forty years. I never went to school, but I know this soil and this weather better than any book. With nine people in my household, grain comes first—we need to eat, and we need steady income. Some of my family work off-farm, so labor is tight during the busy seasons. I have a well, which means I can irrigate when the rain fails, and that gives me some security.

I will plant **winter wheat** on 10 mu. The wheat went into the ground last autumn with rotary tillage, using improved seed at about 30 jin per mu. Now, at the start of the growing season, I will topdress with compound fertilizer and irrigate three times before the June harvest. I expect about 1,000 jin of wheat per mu if the weather cooperates.

Right after the wheat harvest in early June, I will plant **summer maize** on the same 10 mu. I use hybrid seed because it yields better and resists lodging. To save time and labor when everyone is busy, I plant with no-tillage—just sow directly into the wheat stubble. I will apply compound fertilizer at planting and irrigate twice over the summer. Two pesticide sprays are usually enough for the maize.

The remaining **3.1 mu** I will plant to cotton in the spring. Cotton needs more attention, but it brings good cash. I will rotary-till the plots and plant hybrid cotton seed. Cotton is hungry for fertilizer and needs more sprays—about eight times—to keep the bollworms and aphids away. I will irrigate it three times. I expect around 520 jin of seed cotton per mu.

I keep my inputs at the level that has worked for decades: solid basal fertilizer and timely topdressing, enough water, and pesticides when I see pests starting. I do not take big risks because my family depends on this land.
